excluded.reason: Python package initializer; it has no contest selector entry and is not a contest plugin.

interpretation.selectorAvailability: A selector row means the pinned upstream UI can name and import the plugin; it is not xLog implementation or acceptance evidence.
interpretation.sourceExtraction: Mode, exchange and duplicate policy fields are static observations from each pinned plugin source. Missing or dynamic values remain unresolved.
interpretation.pilotBoundary: Exactly sixteen xLog rule implementations are recorded: six source-derived pilots for CQ WW, CQ WPX, and Oceania DX in CW and SSB; two official-corrected SAC 2026 practice previews in CW and SSB; three official-rules NAQP 2026 plain-logging previews in CW, SSB, and RTTY; one official-rules ARRL RTTY Roundup plain-logging preview; two official-rules ARRL DX practice previews in CW and SSB; and two official-rules JIDX 2026 practice previews in CW and SSB. Evidence is scoped by field and is not current sponsor, application, native-package, submission, full-port, real-radio/keying, full Run/S&P, or operator acceptance.
interpretation.pendingBoundary: pending and unknown fields are deliberate; no acceptance is inferred from source presence, selector presence, shared infrastructure, or another plugin.
interpretation.officialCorrectionBoundary: SAC CW and SSB use the published SAC 2026 rules as operational authority and deliberately correct identified pinned-source defects. They are official-corrected practice and scoring previews, not claims of exact upstream parity or submission readiness.
interpretation.naqpAuthorityBoundary: NAQP CW, SSB, and RTTY use the published NCJ 2026 rules and multiplier form as primary authority. The pinned Python plugins remain compatibility comparators with recorded gaps; their commit is not the NAQP rule sourceRevision. These are plain-logging previews, not claims of exact upstream parity, full operating support, sponsor certification, or submission readiness.
interpretation.arrlRTTYAuthorityBoundary: ARRL RTTY Roundup uses the published ARRL Rules v3.0b plus pinned ARRL/RAC section and current DXCC authority as primary authority. The pinned Python plugin remains a compatibility comparator with recorded gaps; its commit is not the rule sourceRevision. This is a plain-logging preview with versioned Cabrillo and ADIF output, not a claim of full Run/S&P operation, real RTTY generation/keying, category/date/operating-time enforcement, sponsor certification, or submission readiness.
interpretation.jidxAuthorityBoundary: JIDX CW and SSB use the published JIDX 2026-10 rules, multiplier list, electronic-log guide, upload pages, ADIF 3.1.7, and pinned callsign/reference authorities as primary evidence. The pinned Python plugins remain compatibility comparators with recorded scoring, role, multiplier-scope, and export-token gaps; their commit is not the JIDX rule sourceRevision. These are shared-UI practice previews with versioned Cabrillo and ADIF output, not claims of native-package launch, full Run/S&P operation, real radio/keying, full-category enforcement, sponsor certification, or submission readiness.
interpretation.arrlDXAuthorityBoundary: ARRL DX CW and SSB use the published ARRL DX Rules v2.0, pinned US, Canadian, and W/VE multiplier lists, contest-section guidance, current DXCC authority, and supplemental ARRL power-normalization guidance as primary authority. The pinned Python plugins remain compatibility comparators with recorded directional, multiplier, exchange, and export gaps; their commit is not the ARRL DX rule sourceRevision. These are shared-UI practice previews with versioned Cabrillo and ADIF output, not claims of browser-worker Run/S&P, operator-profile coverage, native-package launch, full-category enforcement, cross-platform acceptance, sponsor certification, or submission readiness.

ruleAudit.note: Primary authority is the pinned sponsor rules and supporting multiplier, section, DXCC, and power-normalization material. The Python plugins are compatibility comparators with explicit directional, multiplier, exchange, and export gaps; exact comparator parity is not claimed.

sourceDerivedScoringCases.note: Official direction, exchange, eligibility, three-point, per-band duplicate, and per-band multiplier behavior is tested with explicit pinned-Python differences; this is not a claim of exact comparator parity.

independentScoringCases.note: Independent CW and SSB fixtures prove W/VE score 75 and DX scores 108 then 126, including duplicates and per-band DXCC or W/VE subdivision multipliers; they are not operator acceptance.

mutationRestart.note: Core and store coverage spans both modes and both contest directions. The real worker fixture covers W/VE and DX in CW and SSB through create, two sequential returned-draft commits, reset, commit replay, restart/reopen, received-exchange correction, deletion, and Cabrillo/ADIF export. Its forged correction clears wire consistency and is rejected by the authoritative stored-QSO immutability guard for allocatedSentSerial; this is not isolated directional-validator evidence. Fixture-backed React tests cover four creation/input paths plus partial K/KI/KIL/KILO entry and invalid 2000 then valid 100 correction recovery. No browser-worker Run/S&P or packaged operator lifecycle is evidenced.

exportGoldens.note: Core/export-layer versioned CW and SSB Cabrillo and ADIF goldens cover both directions, section-independent LOCATION, raw and normalized power, bounded over-width power projection, state-versus-power ADIF fields, deterministic order, and strict identities. The real worker fixture exports both formats in all four direction/mode scenarios. Shared-UI export flow, full categories and operator profiles, sponsor validation/upload, and submission readiness remain open.

ruleAudit.note: The JIDX 2026-10 rules, multiplier list, electronic-log guide, upload pages, ADIF 3.1.7, RSGB prefix guidance, and pinned CTY/DXCC data are primary authority. The pinned Python comparator has role-validation, per-band multiplier, Japanese-entity, phone-token, and category/export gaps.

sourceDerivedScoringCases.note: Official CW/phone point weights, JA-versus-DX/MM role validation, per-band duplicate/multiplier scope, and explicit pinned-Python deviations are tested; this is not a claim of exact comparator parity.

independentScoringCases.note: Independent fixtures prove non-JA score 40 and JA score 48 across six band weights, duplicates, Japanese locations, DXCC entities, CQ zones, and maritime-mobile zone-only credit; they are not operator acceptance.

mutationRestart.note: Both modes have core and store coverage. The CW worker covers DX and maritime-mobile create/open/draft/apply/commit/edit/restart and export, with DX deletion and maritime-mobile commit replay; the shared UI covers CW maritime-mobile create/apply/correction only. Single-digit raw evidence such as 3 and 5 remains raw while normalized scoring/Cabrillo projections remain 03 and 05 across the covered returned-draft, correction, reopen, and replay paths. JA/SSB worker coverage is limited to session creation, and client coverage is decode-only.

exportGoldens.note: Core/export-layer versioned CW and Phone Cabrillo and ADIF bytes cover JA, DX, maritime-mobile, leading-zero normalization, deterministic order, and single-band projection.
